chapter: The Latin scene and business of the 1940s-70s
title: Cugat at St. Nicholas Arena

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: You know the one thing that happened, there was a -- something happened to me one day that was, oh, I had to laugh because -- I laughed at that, I did, because it was so -- to me, it was out of place. For the first time in the history of New York, they advertised a big band in the St. Nicole Arena, music.
Xavier Cugat (unintelligible). So we got into that dance.

So Xavier Cugat (unintelligible). We go to this dance and he plays the first set (unintelligible). People are going to be crazy. So when we got through, he say, -- it was an ironical way to say, , we play the music, I have collected a bunch. (Unintelligible.) Like you've got 50 cents and I've got a million dollars. (Unintelligible) I collect and you get nothing.
But those are the kind of things you have to face.
